tape.note: yes_bid==0 and yes_ask==1 are Kalshi empty-book sentinels and are written as blank (absent), never as a price.

corrections.reason: The cited Wayback snapshot 20260728110106 is not retrievable, so the row's provenance could not be verified and the row was dropped by backfill_gas_history.py --regenerate. 2026-07-28 is now a legitimate missing day per data contract 1.1.
evidence: Re-fetching the cited replay URL on 2026-07-29 returns HTTP 200 but serves the 2026-07-27 capture: Memento-Datetime 'Mon, 27 Jul 2026 11:01:14 GMT', final URL https://web.archive.org/web/20260727110114id_/https://gasprices.aaa.com/, 97497 bytes, sha256 6af73873d79d0026f00b0cbe6c3b5fa63b203d8886d3854461cb80c7ef71fc66. That does NOT match the recorded raw_sha256, so the URL resolves while validating the wrong day -- the shape a naive re-check cannot see.

The row was an orphan from an earlier run: the committed backfill_audit.json reported days_present=1550 and listed 2026-07-28 among missing_days while the CSV beside it held 1551 rows including one for that date. First-writer-wins preserved it and nothing re-enumerated it. scripts/backfill_gas_history.py's series_reconciliation block now measures that disagreement on every run.

NOT hidden, because it argues the other way: a local capture cache file named 20260728110106.html does exist outside the repository (under the OS temp dir), its sha256 matches the recorded raw_sha256, it is 95193 bytes -- distinct from both neighbours -- and it parses to Current=4.099 / Yesterday=4.110, which chains correctly against 2026-07-27 (Current 4.110) and 2026-07-29 (Yesterday 4.099). Sibling subresources of that crawl (favicon.ico and a cdn-cgi script at 20260728110109/110110) are still in CDX, so the crawl did happen and was later de-indexed. The value 4.099 is therefore probably correct -- but an uncommitted file in a temp directory is not retrievable provenance, and this series' raw_sha256 column exists so that a third party can re-obtain the bytes. An unverifiable row in a provenance file is worse than an honest gap, so the row went. It was NOT re-derived from the 2026-07-27 capture: that capture carries 07-27's Current value and cannot supply 07-28's.
corrections.note: No provenance URL was invented and no value was substituted. backfill_gas_history.fetch_snapshot now rejects any response whose served capture instant disagrees with the requested timestamp, so this class of row cannot be written again.

items.item: month-end projection MAE on >= 6 held-out month-ends
items.reason: **37 month-ends held out** on the AAA span 2022-01-01 .. 2026-07-29 (1494 usable rows). Reported in §3.1; the clause is MET in §1.

items.item: realized PnL on more than 2 settled `KXAAAGASM` settlement(s)
items.reason: Kalshi prunes settled markets from the public API after roughly two months, so only 3 monthly event(s) are retrievable at all and only 2 of them had settled when the tape was fetched. **A longer AAA backfill does not fix this** — the missing data is exchange-side market history, not price history.
items.closes: record `KXAAAGASM` ladders live from now on. Meanwhile the weekly series supplies 10 settled week-ends as evidence about the *shape*, reported separately in §4.2/§5.2 and never pooled into the monthly headline.

items.item: intra-hour quote path and resting-order queue position
items.reason: the candlesticks endpoint is hourly, so any sub-hour traversal is invisible and queue position is unobservable at any resolution. The maker leg is therefore a bound, not a measurement, which is why §0's verdict is taken from the taker path.
items.closes: record gas ladders live at the Phase 0 harvester's cadence

items.item: an ex-ante argument for one RBOB benchmark over another
items.reason: every NY Harbor *RBOB* series in EIA's bulk archive is a futures series ending 2024-04-05, so the national-benchmark comparison has to be made against conventional-spot series, which are a different product
items.closes: not needed for this verdict — §6.1 recomputes the headline under all three and the realized sign does not depend on the choice
